headline: AI stocks rebound in a short Black Friday
context: Investors returned to beaten-down chip and AI stocks in a half-day session, capping the S&P 500's best week in 19 months.
chart_title: Tech led; all but staples rose

COHR.text: No company news. Optical network stocks bounced back from Wednesday's AI sell-off.

LITE.text: No company news. Rose with network gear makers as AI stocks recovered; Arista also gained.

STX.text: Storage and memory stocks rallied together as buyers returned to AI names, with Western Digital also up sharply.

VRTX.text: The FDA delayed its decision on povetacicept, a kidney disease drug, to as late as 28 February.

PODD.text: No company news. Health care lagged the rally, and fellow device makers Baxter and ResMed also slipped.

SJM.text: No company news. Packaged food makers fell together, with Hormel and General Mills also lower.

watch.title: Marvell earnings
watch.text: A key AI chip maker reports, days after a rocky week for the sector.

watch.title: November jobs report
watch.text: The monthly hiring figures land at 8:30am ET.

question: Was this week's AI rebound the real thing, or just a breather?
